arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Stearns argued that the Court should treat pendent party jurisdiction as a logical extension of prior law.
Mr. Phillips cited the Zahn decision to support the view that class actions require all members to meet the amount requirement.
Justice Stevens questioned why the minimum remedy is not simply dismissing non-qualifying parties.
Justice O'Connor suggested that the statute implies the court has jurisdiction over the action but not defective claims.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of federal diversity jurisdiction. The core issue is how courts handle mixed claims where some meet the statutory amount threshold and others do not. The Court must define the proper procedural remedy for these jurisdictional defects.

paragraphs: This dispute defines the limits of federal court power over mixed claims. It determines how judges manage cases with varying claim values. The outcome shapes procedural efficiency and fairness for litigants nationwide. It clarifies the balance between statutory text and practical case management.
